docs: adapters.md documents an engine= keyword that the LangGraph, OpenAI and LangChain adapters reject — open-source issue in Cyrax321/CONTINUUM. Labels: documentation, good first issue, adapter. ## Summary

summary: This open-source documentation issue points out an inconsistency: the project's documentation incorrectly states that an `engine=` keyword can be used with certain AI agent adapters (like those for LangGraph, OpenAI, and LangChain), even though the code for these adapters doesn't support it. Good documentation is incredibly important for any software project, especially in complex areas like AI agents and MLOps, as it helps developers understand and use the tools correctly. Fixing such discrepancies improves the overall developer experience and prevents frustration. This is a great 'good first issue' to get involved in open-source and appreciate the value of clear technical communication. You could investigate the code for one of the mentioned adapters to confirm the keyword's absence.
why: A good first open-source contribution to improve documentation for AI agent integration.

title: GenAI RAG Tutorial Build PDF Question Answering System with FAISS & OpenAI using LangChain Framework
author: Mithilesh yadav
raw_text: In this GenAI and LangChain RAG tutorial, we will build a complete PDF Question Answering system using LangChain, OpenAI ...
summary: This youtube tutorial guides you through building a complete pdf question-answering system using retrieval-augmented generation (rag). it leverages the langchain framework, openai's language models, and faiss for efficient similarity search. you'll learn how to process pdf documents, create embeddings, store them in a vector database like faiss, and then retrieve relevant information to augment llm responses. this project is a fantastic way to see how multiple genai components come together to solve a real-world problem. understanding this workflow is key for developing intelligent applications. you could follow this tutorial to build your own pdf q&a system, gaining hands-on experience with rag and langchain.
why: Hands-on RAG tutorial, combining LLMs, LangChain, and vector databases for practical use.

title: OpenAI LLM Generator (adaumsilva/RAG-framework)
raw_text:
OpenAI LLM Generator — open-source issue in adaumsilva/RAG-framework. Labels: enhancement, good first issue. ## Description

Add `OpenAIGenerator` and/or `AnthropicGenerator` that format retrieved chunks as context and call the respective chat completion API to produce a grounded answer.

## Motivation

`EchoGenerator` is a placeholder that just returns the retrieved text. Real applications need an LLM to synthesise a coherent answer from the retrieved context. This is the final piece needed for a fully functional RAG pipeline.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `OpenAIGenerator` in `ragframework/generator
summary: This open-source issue is about adding an `openaigenerator` to a retrieval-augmented generation (rag) framework. In a rag system, after relevant information is retrieved, an llm needs to synthesize a coherent answer from that context. This generator would take the retrieved chunks and use the openai chat completion api to produce the final, grounded response. This is a critical piece for building functional rag applications and ai agents, as the current placeholder only returns raw text. Understanding and implementing this component helps you grasp the full lifecycle of a rag system, from retrieval to intelligent generation. You could try to build a simple version of this generator yourself, focusing on how to format context for an llm.
why: Implement the LLM generation component within a RAG framework.

title: OpenAI lost the plot on boring LLM use cases (2025)
author: softwaredoug
summary: This headline suggests a critical perspective, implying that OpenAI might be focusing too much on groundbreaking or flashy applications of large language models, potentially overlooking more practical, everyday, or "boring" use cases. While pushing the boundaries of AI is exciting, many real-world problems can be effectively solved with simpler, more robust, and often less complex LLM implementations. For you, this is an important reminder to balance your interest in cutting-edge research with the value of developing reliable tools for common tasks. There's significant opportunity in making AI accessible and useful for everyday scenarios. Try thinking about a mundane task you do and how an LLM could simplify it.
why: Practical LLM applications often solve real problems, not just flashy ones.
